A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAP research despite the changed title and formatting. All 29 pages of v1 and 26 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–G, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original RAP-LLaVA and RAP-Phi3-V experiments on captioning, question answering, recognition, retrieval and ablations, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds retrieval-only baseline results, text-information ablations and standard caption-quality scores.

M1.justification: The database, detection and retrieval procedure, personalized instruction tuning and generation method remain unchanged. Expanded tokenization explanations and the noise-concept illustration document components already described in v1.

E1.justification: Training sources and the 260K dataset composition are unchanged, as are the personalized captioning, question-answering, recognition, MMMU and InfoSeek coverage. V2's standard caption metrics evaluate existing captioning coverage; they do not establish a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: V2 adds LLaVA + Retriever to the quantitative captioning and question-answering/recognition comparisons in Tables 3–4. Existing comparators remain; MyVLM becoming MyVLM-LLaVA in Table 3 is a naming clarification.

E3.justification: V2 adds BLEU-1–4, METEOR, ROUGE-L, CIDEr and SPICE evaluation using five augmented reference captions per image, plus a control omitting concept text. The stated recognition prompt changes from 'single word or phrase' to 'single word'; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds an ablation testing the contribution of additional concept text across captioning, question answering and recognition (Tables 5 and 7). Existing retrieval, dataset-component and database-size analyses remain. Timing and general-knowledge evaluations are relocated to Appendix B.

E5.justification: Both versions report three captioning evaluations with different seeds and average results. V2's new caption-metric table follows the same three-evaluation averaging practice. No new uncertainty estimates or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: V2 adds results including LLaVA + Retriever caption F1 of 2.450, no-text RAP-LLaVA caption F1 of 91.68, and the standard caption scores in Table 8. Existing scores remain unchanged, including RAP-LLaVA caption F1 of 94.97 and question-answering/recognition averages of 0.936/0.980.

T1.justification: The Euclidean retrieval calculation and autoregressive generation factorization retain their substance. V2 changes symbols and abbreviates conditioning in Equation 1, without adding or substantively revising assumptions, theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions retain the RAP framework, personalization dataset, adaptation without further per-concept training, and personalized-performance claims. The general-knowledge claim omitted from v2's shorter conclusion remains in Appendix B.1 with its existing evidence.

C2.justification: V2 interprets retrieval-only failures as supporting personalization training, explains how concept text supplies nonvisual attributes, and discusses general caption quality in Appendix B.3. Appendix F's limitations concerning generation overhead and retrieval accuracy remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 newly states the total of 1,182 caption-evaluation images, explicitly identifies question-answering accuracy, and adds backbone identifiers to Table 4. The code/data/model access pointer changes from a repository to a project page. Principal hardware, hyperparameters and retrieval implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds six supporting references, including Phi-3, BLIP-2, BLIP-Diffusion, InstantBooth, InternVideo2 and personalized video-to-text research. The positioning relative to MyVLM, Yo'LLaVA and retrieval-augmented generation remains essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, lightly edits prose and notation, expands selected explanations, and reorganizes Appendix B to include timing and general-benchmark discussions. The main section sequence and most narrative and appendix text remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reformats the document into two columns and resizes and redistributes displays. Figure 3 adds a noise-concept illustration, several tables gain rows or columns, and a new caption-metric table appears. The timing plot and general-benchmark table move to the appendix.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the evidence with a retrieval-only baseline, text-information ablations and caption-quality metrics, making the contributions of personalization training and descriptions easier to assess. These address gaps in v1 without changing its headline results. The new caption metrics show mixed comparisons with vanilla LLaVA and retain mean-only reporting, limiting the strength of the quality-preservation interpretation.
